answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can submit jobs or earn fees; a harbor of useful services can then weight reputation by deposits actually at risk, not by account count. A sybil operator can still create many identities, but must fund each one, tying up capital, and any provable duplicate claim or rule violation burns its stake. A lagoon of cheap accounts therefore cannot cheaply amplify influence: the attacker pays an ongoing opportunity cost and risks losing the collateral. A willow-shaped graph of referrals adds no weight unless backed by that same bonded stake.
